content.value_statement: Teams need a simple way to move Markdown content between local files and Lark Drive. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through lark-cli shortcuts to create, fetch, and overwrite native Markdown files.
actual_capabilities: Create native Markdown files in Lark Drive from inline content, local files, or stdin.
Fetch a Markdown file from Lark Drive by file token.
Save fetched Markdown content to a chosen local path.
Overwrite an existing Lark Drive Markdown file with new content.
Preview create, fetch, and overwrite requests with dry-run examples.
Enforce Markdown-specific boundaries such as .md file names and native Markdown storage.
limitations: Requires lark-cli and the shared Lark authentication setup.
Handles native Markdown files, not imported Lark docx documents.
Does not manage rename, move, delete, search, permissions, or comments.
Local file reads and writes depend on user-provided paths and CLI validation.

use_cases.title: Publish Team Notes
use_cases.description: Create Markdown files in Lark Drive from prepared release notes, meeting notes, or internal guides.

use_cases.title: Sync Repository Docs
use_cases.description: Upload local README or runbook files to Lark Drive while keeping Markdown as the source format.

use_cases.title: Update Shared Procedures
use_cases.description: Overwrite an existing Markdown file in Lark Drive after confirming the target file token and content source.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New File
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a native Markdown file named README.md in Lark Drive with this content: # Project Notes

prompt_templates.title: Fetch Markdown Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the Lark Drive Markdown file with this file token and show me the content before saving anything locally.

prompt_templates.title: Save a Remote File
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch this Lark Drive Markdown file and save it to ./downloads/. Confirm before overwriting any existing file.

prompt_templates.title: Overwrite with Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Overwrite this Lark Drive Markdown file from ./README.md. Use a dry run first, then ask for confirmation before the final overwrite.

output_examples.input: Create a Markdown file named README.md from local content.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares the create action, checks the .md suffix, and reports the new file token and file name after success.

output_examples.input: Fetch a Lark Drive Markdown file and save it locally.
output_examples.output: The assistant retrieves the file by token, writes it to the requested path, and reports the saved location and file size.

output_examples.input: Overwrite an existing Markdown file after a dry run.
output_examples.output: The assistant previews the overwrite request, asks for confirmation, then reports the updated file name, version, and size.

best_practices: Confirm authentication and target folder or file tokens before running Lark Drive actions.
Use dry-run previews before overwrite operations or bot-owned create operations.
Ask for explicit confirmation before overwriting local files or remote Markdown files.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to import Markdown as a Lark docx document.
Do not use this skill for rename, move, delete, search, permission, or comment workflows.
Do not overwrite a remote file when the file token or source content is uncertain.

faq.question: What type of files does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages native Markdown files stored as ordinary files in Lark Drive.

faq.question: Can it import Markdown into a Lark docx document?
faq.answer: No. Use the Lark Drive import workflow for docx conversion instead.

faq.question: Can it read a Markdown file from Lark Drive?
faq.answer: Yes. It can fetch content by file token and optionally save it to a local path.

faq.question: Can it overwrite an existing Markdown file?
faq.answer: Yes. It can overwrite a native Markdown file when you provide the target file token and new content.

faq.question: Does it require local tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires lark-cli and the Lark authentication setup described by the shared Lark skill instructions.

faq.question: Does it manage Lark permissions?
faq.answer: No. Permission workflows are outside this skill and should use the Lark Drive skill.
